The faction purges its Firmament sheet, leaders, planets, and note for the Obsidian package; the home system and in-play plots flip and ready if controlled. The hosts’ practical line is to place it on the Leadership player with the Firmament hero immediately before flipping, if Leadership remains unplayed, to try for three extra tokens. If Leadership has already resolved or is likely to resolve before the hero, they recommend ignoring this plot; the token payoff is not reliable.

claims.statement: The early secret-objective engine depends on turn order and cooperation. Firmament can copy a secret already scored by another player if it meets the requirement, placing a plot with that player’s token rather than earning a point. Because initiative order determines whose secret becomes available first, scoring after another player can create a plot sooner; Leadership may score before a target, while Imperial can put Firmament later. Share secret information and negotiate reciprocal disclosure or the note when useful, but assess the secret and Sieve risk rather than assuming every secret should be exposed.

claims.statement: Plane Splitter can open a fracture, but inspect who benefits first. Research it while still Firmament: gaining the technology puts the fracture into play and distributes ingress tokens to Mecatol Rex or Thunder’s Edge (if present) and to technology-skip systems. The hosts favor researching it late before the flip if the fracture has not appeared, so the board and likely recipients are clearer. They caution that movement factions may exploit the new access more easily than Firmament; a slice without useful skips or a hostile ingress allocation weakens the plan.

The Obsidian side cannot be researched, so hosts advise researching it as Firmament first; gaining it by another effect after flipping gives only the Obsidian side, not the fracture-opening effect. They suggest reclaiming a route or denying a leader’s route to the fracture; movement and access remain prerequisites.

The Firmament side can add one infantry to a controlled home-system planet at Status Phase while Obsidian is in play; hosts question the value of investing in this before a flip. Obsidian instead destroys another player’s infantry in or adjacent to a system containing yours at the start of your turn. They warn that repeatedly targeting one neighbor can provoke heat and leave that player unable to participate, without advancing your own win. They mainly consider researching it for the fracture-opening effect of an Entropic Scar.

Their default is Antimass Deflectors or Dark Energy Tap, Gravity Drive, Carrier II, Dreadnought II, and Fleet Logistics as needed. A more adventurous green/yellow route can cover Plane Splitter and other options if a target’s future research is dependable. They warn against relying on Extract for core blue prerequisites if the chosen player already owns or is unlikely to research them; establish movement and a viable blue route first.

claims.statement: Sharsiss Hollow can refresh the Obsidian economy. The Obsidian hero readies all planets and is purged. On the flip round, the home system can be spent before the flip, readied by the flip ability, spent again, then readied again by the hero and spent a third time. This is a strong resource burst when timed early enough to use it, though the hosts note a late flip can leave more resources than there are useful actions. Extract is one outlet for the resulting resources.

claims.statement: Myru Vos’s Firmament form helps movement and secrets; Vos Hollow has different timing. The Firmament agent can protect moving ships from Space Cannon when they are not transporting units and can let them pass through enemy ships; hosts report selling this to Ral Nel for a high-movement destroyer play, but say the use is situational. After flipping, Vos Hollow can force an opponent to destroy another ship of the same type during a combat elsewhere. It offers surprise targeted attrition, but both forms are matchup-dependent and the hosts disagree over which side they would rather retain.

claims.statement: Preserve Firmament mechs when their defensive role still matters. Viper EX-23 permits coexisting ground forces when units are committed to the planet; if still coexisting when it flips, control transfers and the other player’s units become the coexisting ones. The hosts value Firmament’s version as a difficult-to-take home-system defense and see a very narrow offensive use: take a key planet, flip, and exploit the changed control—potentially with Imperial. This is a late-flip incentive, not a routine capture plan.

claims.statement: Do not build the Obsidian flagship for its extra die alone. Heaven’s Eye has the more useful plot-dependent movement and repair text, while its Obsidian side gains a die but loses that text. The hosts question its value given the faction’s economy, and say a War Sun may offer more practical functionality in an unusually rich game. The Firmament flagship may be attractive only if its text is central to a plan; otherwise the build is hard to justify.

claims.statement: Fracture access and movement shape the draft. The hosts want a nearby Scar and a green or yellow skip as optional support for Plane Splitter, while advising against treating that line as guaranteed. In most games they return to blue movement and fleet technology; if Extract reliably supplies blue tech, a green/yellow route becomes more plausible. Slice, table technology choices, and actual ingress placement decide which plan is safe.

claims.conditions: At the flip decision: round three is the repeatable host default, with earlier or later timing only for a concrete payoff.
claims.statement: The timing disagreement remains real. One host’s abstract advice moves toward flipping early so plots operate longer and the Obsidian hero can recycle planets; the other favors round three after two public scores, a personal secret, and preferably both Siphon and Extract. Round two is an exceptional payoff line; round four may make sense for a specific Sieve or mech use, or Plane Splitter timing, but risks missing economic benefits. Round-one wins are acknowledged but not treated as repeatable evidence.
